content.title: About
content.content: Split pea soup is made from yellow or green dried peas, water, vegetables, and seasonings. It has a thick, creamy texture and a hearty aroma typical of traditional Northern European and American cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The soup is often served with smoked ham or bacon to deepen the flavor.
Traditional split pea soup is a national dish of the Netherlands (Erwtensoep) and the United States (Pea Soup).
Dried peas are split in half, which speeds up cooking and creates a smoother consistency.
It is commonly prepared in large batches and frozen – the taste improves after reheating.
Some recipes add carrots, leeks, and celery for extra brightness.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peas provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g of dry product, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas contain thiamine, folate, and vitamin B6, important for metabolism.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Peas supply iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and zinc, supporting blood health and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Split pea soup contains virtually no saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause increased gas in sensitive people.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Peas contain purines, so people with gout should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot, often with a slice of rye bread or croutons. It can be made ahead, stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, or frozen for up to 3 months.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dried peas in a cool, dry place in an airtight container. Store prepared soup in a sealed container in the fridge, and freeze in portion‑size containers for longer storage.
